newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Puerto Rico blast search ends as building shifts.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico blast search ends as building shifts.

text.p: Five more bodies were found on Sunday in the rubble of a building devastated by a suspected gas explosion, but searchers stopped work when the teetering building shifted, authorities said.

The discoveries brought to 27 the number of victims found. Searchers suspect there may be as many as 20 additional corpses in the ruins. At least 80 other people were injured in the blast on Thursday.
The search for bodies was halted once on Sunday when an impromptu prayer service was piped to the site from a church across the street and again late in the day when the building shifted.
Officials said they would bring in structural engineers to make a safety assessment before restarting the search.

Crews resumed combing through the tangled wreckage on Saturday after being forced to wait more than 40 hours while sagging floors and walls were reinforced. Dogs trained to sniff out survivors found no signs of life when the search resumed.
The searchers included rescue teams from Miami and New York.

The six-story Humberto Vidal building, housing a shoe store, a jewelry store and offices above, was devastated by an explosion that occurred just as the working day was beginning in Calle de Diego, a shopping street in San Juan's working-class Rio Piedras district.
Federal investigators, including experts from the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, have come to the site.
During a visit on Saturday, Gov. Pedro Rossello said the evidence pointed to a gas leak but it would be a week or more before investigators could determine the cause of the explosion.
